entities.summary: Albert of Stade was a German monk, historian, and poet who lived in the 13th century. He is best known for his chronicle of the history of the Archdiocese of Bremen, which provides valuable insights into the social, political, and religious landscape of medieval Germany. The chronicle was written in Latin and consists of 17 chapters, covering the period from the 8th to the 12th centuries. Albert's work is significant not only for its historical value but also for its poetic style, which is notable for its use of alliteration and assonance. The chronicle has been widely studied and translated, and its contents are now preserved in several manuscripts held in libraries across Europe. The legacy of Albert of Stade can be seen in the many historical accounts and chronicles that followed in his footsteps, and his work continues to be an important source of information for historians and scholars of medieval Germany.
